ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$ and $\angle B=45^\circ$. A line is drawn through point A such that $AD \parallel BC$, with point D to the right of point A. Points P and Q are located on ray $AD$ and ray $CB$, respectively. Point E is a point on line segment $CQ$, and $CQ=2AP$. Let $AP=x$ and $CE=y$, then $y=2x-2$. When point Q is the midpoint of $BC$, $y=3$. If $PE \perp BC$, find the length of $BQ$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the diagram, draw $AM\perp BC$ at point M, PE intersects AC at point N,\\
$\because$ $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, $\angle B=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle C=180^\circ-\angle BAC-\angle B=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B=\angle C$, $BM=MC=\frac{1}{2}BC=\frac{1}{2}\times 10=5$,\\
$\because$ $AM\perp BC$, $PE\perp BC$,\\
$\therefore$ $AM\parallel PE$,\\
Also, $\because$ $AD\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral AMEP is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$ $ME=AP=x$,\\
$\because$ $CE=y=2x-2$,\\
From $MC=CE+ME$, we get, $5=2x-2+x$,\\
Solving yields $x=\frac{7}{3}$, that is $AP=\frac{7}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ $CQ=2AP=2\times \frac{7}{3}=\frac{14}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ $BQ=BC-CQ=10-\frac{14}{3}=\boxed{\frac{16}{3}}$;

From the text, use the special midpoint case to determine BC: when Q is midpoint, y=3 and y=2x-2 give x=5/2, so CQ=2AP=5; since CQ is then half of BC, BC=10. 设 B=(0,0)，C=(10,0)。因为 ∠BAC=90°，∠B=45°，所以 ∠C=45°，△ABC 是等腰直角三角形，A 位于 BC 的中垂线上，且高为 BC/2=5，所以 A=(5,5)。由于 AD∥BC，AD 是水平线 y=5；AP=x，因此 P=(5+x,5)。又 PE⊥BC，BC 是 x 轴，所以 E 是 P 竖直向下在 x 轴上的点，即 E=(5+x,0)。于是 CE=10-(5+x)=5-x。

题中 CE=y=2x-2，所以 5-x=2x-2，解得 3x=7，即 x=7/3。于是 CQ=2AP=2x=14/3。最后 BQ=BC-CQ=10-14/3=16/3。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$ and $\angle B=45^\circ$. A line is drawn through point A such that $AD \parallel BC$, with point D to the right of point A. Points P and Q are located on ray $AD$ and ray $CB$, respectively. Point E is a point on line segment $CQ$, and $CQ=2AP$. Let $AP=x$ and $CE=y$, then $y=2x-2$. When point Q is the midpoint of $BC$, $y=3$. If $PE \perp BC$, find the length of $BQ$.
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the diagram, draw $AM\perp BC$ at point M, PE intersects AC at point N,\\
$\because$ $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, $\angle B=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle C=180^\circ-\angle BAC-\angle B=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B=\angle C$, $BM=MC=\frac{1}{2}BC=\frac{1}{2}\times 10=5$,\\
$\because$ $AM\perp BC$, $PE\perp BC$,\\
$\therefore$ $AM\parallel PE$,\\
Also, $\because$ $AD\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral AMEP is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$ $ME=AP=x$,\\
$\because$ $CE=y=2x-2$,\\
From $MC=CE+ME$, we get, $5=2x-2+x$,\\
Solving yields $x=\frac{7}{3}$, that is $AP=\frac{7}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ $CQ=2AP=2\times \frac{7}{3}=\frac{14}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ $BQ=BC-CQ=10-\frac{14}{3}=\boxed{\frac{16}{3}}$;
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the base BC of triangle ABC is horizontal, B is on the left, C is on the right, and A is above; there is a right-angle mark at A. Draw a horizontal line AD to the right through A, parallel to BC, and P is on AD. On the base, from left to right, B, Q, E, C can be seen, and E is located on segment CQ. Reasoning: First use the special situation given in the problem to determine BC. If Q is the midpoint of BC, and y=3, also y=2x-2, so 3=2x-2, solving gives x=5/2. Because CQ=2AP=2x, at this time CQ=5. When Q is the midpoint of BC, CQ=BC/2, therefore BC=10. Now construct AM⊥BC, with foot M. Because ∠BAC=90°, ∠B=45°, so ∠C=45°, triangle ABC is an isosceles right triangle, and the altitude AM from A to the hypotenuse BC falls on the midpoint M of BC, hence MC=BC/2=5. Also because PE⊥BC, AM⊥BC, so PE∥AM; and AD∥BC, so AP∥ME. Therefore quadrilateral AMEP is a parallelogram, obtaining ME=AP=x. From the figure, E is between M and C, MC=ME+CE=x+y. The problem gives y=2x-2, so 5=x+(2x-2)=3x-2, solving gives x=7/3. Thus CQ=2AP=2x=14/3, hence BQ=BC-CQ=10-14/3=16/3.
